Reason for consultation: The patient, a 40 -year -old woman, goes to the consultation for presenting the distal phalanx of the fifth toe, mucopolysaccharide storage syndrome and choriorretian coloboma. Diagnosis: After the evaluation of the symptoms and the results of the exams performed, the diagnosis of Hurler Syndrome is established, a form of mucopolysacaridosis of type I, which is characterized by the deficiency of an enzyme that breaks down the mucopolysaccharides, which leads to its accumulation in different tissues. This syndrome can manifest itself with fusion of phalanges, ocular alterations such as choriorretian coloboma, as well as other systemic symptoms.

Treatment: Hurler syndrome treatment includes enzymatic replacement therapies, surgical interventions to correct bone deformities, as well as ophthalmological monitoring to control possible visual complications.

Recommendations: The patient is recommended to maintain periodic medical follow -up, follow the treatment for the medical team and go to follow -up consultations with the corresponding specialists.
